praxis-special-education-readiness-check.prompt: At the annual IEP meeting, a general educator asks which pieces of content federal law actually requires in the document. Which set belongs in the IEP?

options.a: Present levels, a medical diagnosis code, and the teacher's daily lesson plans
options.b: Measurable annual goals, full-scale IQ scores, and the student's class schedule
options.c: Short-term objectives for every IEP and a schoolwide discipline contract
options.d: Present levels, measurable annual goals, services, and educational placement

praxis-special-education-readiness-check.explanation: IDEA requires an IEP to state present levels of academic and functional performance, measurable annual goals, the special education and related services to be provided, and the student's educational placement (including LRE). Diagnosis codes, IQ composites, and daily lesson plans live in evaluation reports or teacher planning, not as required IEP content. Short-term objectives are required when the student takes alternate assessments, not for every IEP.

distractorExplanations.a: A medical diagnosis code and lesson plans are not required IEP elements; present levels must be paired with goals, services, and placement.
distractorExplanations.b: IQ scores belong in the evaluation, and a class schedule is not a federal IEP component even when goals are measurable.
distractorExplanations.c: Benchmarks or short-term objectives are required for alternate-assessment students; a schoolwide contract is not an IEP-required element.

praxis-special-education-readiness-check.prompt: A student can access grade-level content with supports, but a parent asks for a self-contained class because 'that is where special education happens.' What does LRE require the team to do?

options.a: Educate alongside nondisabled peers to the maximum extent appropriate
options.b: Place every IEP student full time in general education with no pull-out
options.c: Choose the most specialized classroom the district currently operates
options.d: Assign the closest school that still has an open special education seat

praxis-special-education-readiness-check.explanation: Least restrictive environment means students with disabilities are educated with nondisabled peers to the maximum extent appropriate, with supplementary aids and a continuum of placements. Self-contained is not the default because the student has a disability. Full-time general education with zero pull-out is also not automatic; the team individualizes. Seat availability and concentrating all specialized services are not the LRE test.

distractorExplanations.b: That is full inclusion without a continuum; LRE allows pull-out or a more restrictive setting when data show it is necessary.
distractorExplanations.c: Starting from the most specialized classroom reverses the LRE presumption of general education with supports first.
distractorExplanations.d: Proximity and open seats may be logistics, but LRE is about access to nondisabled peers and appropriate services, not vacancies.

praxis-special-education-readiness-check.prompt: A seventh grader can meet grade-level math standards if given a calculator and extended time. How should the case manager classify those supports?

options.a: They lower the grade-level expectations the student must meet on the test
options.b: They change access to the work without changing grade-level standards
options.c: They cut the number of grade-level standards the student must learn
options.d: They belong on IEPs and cannot be written into a Section 504 plan

praxis-special-education-readiness-check.explanation: Accommodations change how a student accesses instruction or demonstrates learning (calculator, extra time, large print) without changing the grade-level standard being measured. Modifications change what is taught or expected, such as reducing standards or lowering the performance criterion. The same access supports can appear on an IEP or a Section 504 plan.

distractorExplanations.a: Lowering the expectation or the standard being measured is a modification, not an accommodation.
distractorExplanations.c: Dropping standards from the student's curriculum changes content, which is a modification rather than an access support.
distractorExplanations.d: Section 504 plans commonly list accommodations; they are not reserved for IEPs.

praxis-special-education-readiness-check.prompt: Office referrals describe shouting during independent work. Staff want a BIP written from those referrals this week. What should the behavior plan rest on?

options.a: The schoolwide discipline matrix applied uniformly to every referred student
options.b: The topography of the shouting as written on the office referral forms
options.c: An FBA that identifies the function the shouting serves for the student
options.d: The psychiatric diagnosis listed on the student's eligibility paperwork

praxis-special-education-readiness-check.explanation: A Behavior Intervention Plan is individualized and is built from a Functional Behavioral Assessment. The FBA identifies antecedents, consequences, and the function (escape, attention, tangible, sensory) so replacement skills and prevention strategies match why the behavior occurs. Referral topography, a universal matrix, and a diagnosis do not identify function.

distractorExplanations.a: A schoolwide matrix is Tier 1 discipline; a BIP is student-specific and cannot be copied from the code of conduct.
distractorExplanations.b: Topography describes what the behavior looks like; without function, the plan treats form rather than the maintaining consequence.
distractorExplanations.d: Eligibility or a psychiatric label does not tell the team why shouting occurs in independent work; FBA data do.

praxis-special-education-readiness-check.prompt: A student's IEP fluency goal is due on the next periodic progress report. Which monitoring approach should the special educator use?

options.a: Collect one fluency probe at the annual IEP and report that single score
options.b: Use report-card grades that blend effort, behavior, and achievement
options.c: Probe weekly but store graphs in a private file rather than reporting to parents
options.d: Use frequent CBM probes tied to the goal and change instruction from the data

praxis-special-education-readiness-check.explanation: Progress on IEP goals is measured with frequent, goal-aligned tools such as curriculum-based measurement. The data are used to keep or change instruction, and IDEA requires that progress be reported to parents on a periodic schedule (often with report cards). A once-a-year probe, a composite grade, or graphs withheld from families do not meet that duty.

distractorExplanations.a: Annual-only data cannot guide instruction during the year and is too thin for required periodic progress reports.
distractorExplanations.b: Grades mix effort and conduct with achievement; they are not a direct measure of the fluency goal.
distractorExplanations.c: IDEA requires reporting IEP progress to parents; keeping probes in a private teacher file withholds required information.

praxis-special-education-readiness-check.prompt: A principal calls a class 'co-taught' because a special educator consults weekly and a paraprofessional remains in the room. Which arrangement is actually a co-teaching model?

options.a: One teach/one assist, stations, parallel, alternative, and team teaching
options.b: Push-in tutoring, pull-out resource, and self-contained as co-teach types
options.c: Consultation in which the special educator advises but does not instruct
options.d: Para-led instruction while the special educator plans in another room

praxis-special-education-readiness-check.explanation: Co-teaching is two certified teachers sharing instruction in the same general education class. Common models are one teach/one assist (or one observe), station teaching, parallel teaching, alternative (differentiated) teaching, and team teaching. Consultation, pull-out/self-contained placements, and para-led coverage are service or staffing arrangements, not co-teaching models.

distractorExplanations.b: Push-in tutoring, resource pull-out, and self-contained describe placements or service delivery, not two teachers sharing one class.
distractorExplanations.c: Consultation is an indirect service; the special educator is not co-delivering instruction in the classroom.
distractorExplanations.d: A paraprofessional providing instruction while the special educator is elsewhere is not co-teaching by two certified teachers.

praxis-special-education-readiness-check.prompt: A parent requests ESY because a sibling attends district summer camp. The team has spring-to-fall skill data. When are ESY services warranted?

options.a: Whenever a parent requests a seat in any summer camp the district happens to run
options.b: When regression and recoupment data show significant skill loss over breaks
options.c: When the student is identified as gifted and has no disability category
options.d: When the team wants summer enrichment unrelated to maintaining FAPE skills

praxis-special-education-readiness-check.explanation: Extended school year is an IEP decision about FAPE, not a summer-camp entitlement. Teams look at likely regression over breaks and how long recoupment would take, along with emerging critical skills. Gifted identification without a disability, parent request alone, and enrichment unrelated to maintaining IEP skills do not establish ESY.

distractorExplanations.a: Parent request for camp does not auto-qualify; ESY is based on individual FAPE data, typically regression and recoupment.
distractorExplanations.c: Gifted students without a disability are not IDEA-eligible for ESY; ESY is an IEP service for students with disabilities.
distractorExplanations.d: Enrichment that is not needed to prevent loss of critical IEP skills is not the ESY standard.

praxis-special-education-readiness-check.prompt: A teacher is designing a science unit for a class that includes students with IEPs. How should Universal Design for Learning shape that unit from the start?

options.a: Wait until the first lesson fails, then add individualized modifications after the fact
options.b: Build the unit around multiple means of grading, retention, and promotion decisions
options.c: Provide multiple means of engagement, representation, and action/expression
options.d: Match each learner to one preferred visual, auditory, or kinesthetic learning style

praxis-special-education-readiness-check.explanation: UDL builds flexibility in at the design stage through three principles: multiple means of engagement (why), representation (what), and action and expression (how). It is proactive for a wide range of learners, not a retrofit after failure, a grading policy, or matching a single supposed learning style.

distractorExplanations.a: Retrofitting modifications after a lesson fails is the opposite of designing flexible options up front.
distractorExplanations.b: Grading, retention, and promotion are school decisions; they are not CAST's three UDL principles.
distractorExplanations.d: Assigning one learning style per student is not UDL and lacks strong evidence; UDL offers multiple options to all learners.

praxis-special-education-readiness-check.prompt: An IEP team is listing related services so the student can benefit from special education. Which services may be included when the team finds they are required?

options.a: Private subject tutoring billed to the district by an outside learning center
options.b: Ongoing physician treatment for the medical condition causing the disability
options.c: Purchase and later surgical replacement of the student's cochlear implant
options.d: Speech-language therapy, occupational therapy, and needed transportation

praxis-special-education-readiness-check.explanation: Related services are developmental, corrective, and supportive services needed for the student to benefit from special education. Speech-language pathology, occupational therapy, and transportation are classic examples when the IEP team determines they are required. IDEA excludes most medical treatment by a physician and surgically implanted devices; private academic tutoring is not a listed related service.

distractorExplanations.a: Outside academic tutoring is not a related service under IDEA; related services support benefit from special education, not private subject coaching.
distractorExplanations.b: Medical services are limited to diagnosis or evaluation that the team needs; ongoing physician treatment is excluded.
distractorExplanations.c: IDEA excludes surgically implanted devices and their optimization or replacement from related services.

praxis-special-education-readiness-check.prompt: Parents ask the district to change placement to a private day school. The IEP team refuses. When must Prior Written Notice be provided?

options.a: When the district proposes or refuses a change in identification, evaluation, or placement
options.b: When the district mails an IEP meeting invitation, before any proposal is made
options.c: When a parent asks under FERPA for a copy of the student's education records
options.d: When a teacher changes seating or a lesson within the current IEP services

praxis-special-education-readiness-check.explanation: Prior Written Notice is required when the district proposes or refuses to initiate or change the student's identification, evaluation, educational placement, or the provision of FAPE. A meeting invitation is a different notice. FERPA governs records access. Day-to-day instructional tweaks inside the current IEP do not trigger PWN.

distractorExplanations.b: A meeting invitation tells parents when the team will meet; PWN follows an actual proposal or refusal to change identification, evaluation, placement, or FAPE.
distractorExplanations.c: A records request is a FERPA access matter, not the PWN trigger.
distractorExplanations.d: Seating or lesson adjustments that stay within the existing IEP are not changes of placement or FAPE requiring PWN.

praxis-special-education-readiness-check.prompt: A draft IEP says the student 'will improve reading this year.' Which rewrite meets SMART annual-goal practice?

options.a: Show stronger reading habits as described in quarterly teacher narratives
options.b: Read 90 WCPM on 4th-grade probes by June on three of four CBM trials
options.c: Feel more confident as a reader on a spring student interest survey
options.d: Finish more ELA packets after the teacher gives daily reminders

praxis-special-education-readiness-check.explanation: Measurable annual goals name the skill, the condition, a criterion, and a timeframe (specific, measurable, achievable, relevant, time-bound). Words-correct-per-minute on specified probes by June with a mastery rule can be graphed and reported. Vague improvement, confidence, or 'more packets' cannot be progress-monitored against a clear standard.

distractorExplanations.a: Teacher narratives about 'stronger habits' are not an objective criterion or a defined skill measure.
distractorExplanations.c: Confidence on a survey is affective and not a measurable academic goal tied to instruction.
distractorExplanations.d: 'More packets' is not a specified rate, accuracy, or date, so it is not a measurable annual goal.

praxis-special-education-readiness-check.prompt: A mixed-ability class is starting the same novel. The teacher wants differentiated instruction rather than a grading shortcut. What does that look like?

options.a: Give every learner identical tasks and identical pacing for the entire unit
options.b: Lock students into ability groups formed on day one for the entire year
options.c: Adjust content, process, product, or environment based on readiness and data
options.d: Raise report-card grades for IEP students so effort replaces the product

praxis-special-education-readiness-check.explanation: Differentiated instruction varies content, process, product, or learning environment using ongoing data on readiness, interest, and learning profile, while students still work toward the same essential understandings. Uniform tasks, year-long ability tracking, and raising grades for effort are not differentiation.

distractorExplanations.a: Identical tasks and pacing are one-size instruction; differentiation changes the path based on learner need.
distractorExplanations.b: Permanent ability groups are tracking; flexible grouping changes as student data change.
distractorExplanations.d: Inflating grades for effort is a grading change, not an instructional adjustment of content, process, or product.

praxis-special-education-readiness-check.prompt: A student with an IEP is on the 11th consecutive school day of out-of-school suspension for the same code of conduct. What must the team complete?

options.a: No meeting yet; manifestation review waits until 5 consecutive removal days
options.b: A manifestation meeting, because any short suspension of any length requires one
options.c: A reevaluation, because a parent request after the incident is the trigger
options.d: A manifestation determination, because this removal is a change of placement

praxis-special-education-readiness-check.explanation: A disciplinary change of placement occurs when a removal is more than 10 consecutive school days, or when a series of removals is a pattern. That change of placement requires a manifestation determination within 10 school days of the decision. Five days is the wrong threshold; brief removals that are not a pattern do not require MDR; a parent reevaluation request is a separate process.

distractorExplanations.a: The consecutive-day trigger is more than 10 school days, not 5.
distractorExplanations.b: Removals of 10 days or fewer that are not a pattern do not require a manifestation determination.
distractorExplanations.c: A parent request starts evaluation timelines; manifestation review is triggered by a disciplinary change of placement.

praxis-special-education-readiness-check.prompt: A 16-year-old's IEP is due. The vocational coordinator asks what IDEA transition services must be oriented toward.

options.a: Postsecondary education, employment, and independent living after high school
options.b: Accruing every academic credit required for a standard high school diploma this year
options.c: The building move from middle-school teams into high-school course registration
options.d: Completing guardianship petitions and adult SSI paperwork as the primary goal

praxis-special-education-readiness-check.explanation: Beginning by age 16 (earlier if the team decides), the IEP includes measurable postsecondary goals and transition services that are results-oriented toward post-school education or training, employment, and where appropriate independent living. Diploma credits and grade-to-grade moves matter for school programming, but they are not the IDEA definition of transition. Guardianship and benefits may be discussed; they are not the core of transition services.

distractorExplanations.b: Credit accrual supports a diploma but is not the results-oriented post-school focus of IDEA transition services.
distractorExplanations.c: Changing buildings or grade bands is an in-school transition, not postsecondary transition under IDEA.
distractorExplanations.d: Legal and benefits paperwork may be a family topic; IDEA transition centers on postsecondary education, work, and independent living skills.

praxis-special-education-readiness-check.prompt: During an IEP for SLD in written expression, a team member says assistive technology consideration is limited to physical or sensory disabilities. What is the team's duty?

options.a: Wait for a physician prescription before the team may discuss any AT device
options.b: Consider whether assistive technology is required for FAPE for every IEP student
options.c: Limit AT discussion to students with orthopedic or sensory impairments
options.d: Require the family to purchase and maintain any device they want used at home and school

praxis-special-education-readiness-check.explanation: IDEA requires the IEP team to consider the student's need for assistive technology devices and services in every IEP, including for SLD in writing (for example, speech-to-text). Need is an IEP-team FAPE decision, not a physician prescription, not limited to physical/sensory eligibility, and not shifted to the family as a purchase requirement when AT is needed for FAPE.

distractorExplanations.a: A doctor's prescription is not the gate for school AT; the IEP team decides whether AT is needed for FAPE.
distractorExplanations.c: AT must be considered for every student with an IEP, including learning disabilities, not only orthopedic or sensory impairments.
distractorExplanations.d: If the team determines AT is required for FAPE, the district provides it at no cost, including home use when the IEP requires it.
